newsitem.title: ITALY: Six groups interested in Banco Napoli.
newsitem.headline: Six groups interested in Banco Napoli.

text.p: Three Italian and three foreign institutions have expressed an interest in the sale of 60 percent of stock in Banco di Napoli, the southern Italian bank said in a statement.
It said the names of the companies and groups involved would not be released. Interested parties have until December 20 to make offers for the majority stake in the struggling bank.
Italy's Treasury-controlled Banca Nazionale di Lavoro and insurer INA said on Monday they had expressed joint interest in Banco di Napoli.
No other groups have formally announced an interest.

Italian newspapers reported on Tuesday that Germany's Bayerische Landesbank, Britain's Natwest and the Netherlands' Rabobank were thought to be considering separate bids for control of Banco di Napoli.
Banco di Napoli said the group that offered the highest bid would take the 60 percent stake.

Companies which express an interest in the loss-making Banco di Napoli now have the right to study information being prepared on the bank by merchant bank N.M. Rothschild, which has been retained by the Treasury as an advisor.

Banco di Napoli unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire in 1995 and plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year thanks largely to a poor, highly politicised loan policy.
The Treasury has installed new management at the firm and has promised to take on the bulk of the company's stock of bad debt before selling the group. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
